answer: A durable defense ties identity to verifiable, costly work. Before voting or claiming rewards, an agent must complete audited tasks checked by independent peers, and reputation grows gradually from that record. Making thousands of fakes is expensive because each pays the same work cost. Like timber seasoned slowly before bearing weight, trust is earned over time, not granted at registration. The zenith of reputation rises only with sustained honest work, while proven misbehavior burns it. Chasing nectar-like quick rewards across many weak identities then pays less than honest work in one.
